key_facts: Several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
Several weeks of external deviation of the nasal septum
CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy showed spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components, significant multinucleated giant cells on biopsy, and rare mitotic activity without cytologic atypia are characteristic of Central Giant Cell Granuloma, which is known to cause local bone destruction and remodeling as seen in the CT scan findings.

rejected.label: Ossifying Fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibroma typically presents with a well-defined, fibro-osseous lesion and does not usually exhibit the aggressive features of bony erosion and significant giant cell presence as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors of bone are rare in the maxillary sinus and typically occur in the epiphyseal region of long bones, with a higher rate of mitotic activity and cytologic atypia than observed in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous Dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia is characterized by a ground-glass appearance on imaging and the presence of fibro-osseous tissue without significant giant cell infiltration, which does not match the biopsy and imaging findings of this case.
